concept: Table prints rows of readings the way a service label is printed on the case of an appliance: flat ink on the plastic, one seam cut between rows, figures lined up on their right edge so a column reads as one number. It holds readings and never acts like a control.

default_to_avoid.pattern: zebra-striped data table with a tinted header band, a hover highlight on every row and a full box border
default_to_avoid.why_not: Stripes and hover fills add tints the plastic never had, make rows look pressable when they are not, and the box frame competes with the unit's own edge.

default_to_avoid.pattern: table scrolled sideways inside a div that keyboard users cannot reach
default_to_avoid.why_not: A scroll box with no focus stop hides its overflowing columns from anyone who does not use a pointer.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): station names and bands printed in ruled rows on the case, no fills
system/FORM.md divider class: a seam cut in the plastic, divider tone over the lit edge
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: sortable table, aria-sort on the column header

derivation.consequence: printing is flat on the material, with no shadow and no emboss
derivation.form: Cells carry no fill, no shadow and no raised edge, and the rows are told apart only by a seam between them.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: A numeric column prints in tabular figures and aligns to the end edge, so digits of one place stand in one vertical line.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The first column starts on the unit's inset line with no cell padding, and the caption is printed above it on the same line.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: A sortable header is one key with a visible label, Enter and Space press it, and a scroll region that overflows takes a Tab stop so its columns can be reached.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: Header, seams, sort marks and focus ring are ink, so a Table never spends the unit's one orange.

variants.reason: A is flat printing under P5 and reuses the Divider seam, so rows read as printed lines; B's recessed strip looks like an Input or Display window and invites a press, and C boxes every cell like a spreadsheet and adds more lines than the readings need.

scroll.why: A region that scrolls sideways when the columns are wider than the unit, so no column is cut off and none is squeezed below its words.

root.why: The table fills the width of its column and keeps one grid, so columns line up from the header down to the last row.

caption.why: The caption names the table in small secondary ink above the header, on the inset line like a label printed on the case.

head.why: The header row is printed in the same flat ink as the body and set apart only by a seam below it.

body.why: The body rows stand in a fixed column grid, so a sort changes the order of the rows and nothing reflows.

row.why: A row is a line of printing and takes no fill or hover, because nothing in it can be pressed.

cell.why: A cell keeps even padding and breaks long words, so Thai and long names wrap inside the column and are never clipped.

headCell.why: A column header is printed in medium weight and secondary ink so it reads as a label, one step quieter than the readings.

sortKey.why: A sortable header holds one key that fills the cell, at least 44px tall, so a finger can press it and Enter or Space does the same.

sortMark.why: A chevron shows the sort direction by its shape, and its place is held when the column is not sorted so the header does not shift.

data-numeric.why: A numeric cell or header aligns to the end edge in tabular figures so the digits of one place line up down the column.

aria-sort=ascending.why: The sorted column's label goes to primary ink and shows an up chevron, so direction is a shape and not a colour.

aria-sort=descending.why: The sorted column's label goes to primary ink and shows a down chevron, so direction is a shape and not a colour.

hover.why: Over a sort key the label goes from secondary to primary ink, the same cue Accordion gives its trigger, with no fill.

focus-visible.why: The sort key and a scroll region that has taken a Tab stop show the same ink ring with an offset, so keyboard position is always visible.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the seams draw as a single system-colour line and the sort key keeps a visible focus outline.

color.why: Only the label ink of a sort key changes, over the hover duration, and under Reduce motion it changes at once.
